trust_decision.summary: vimball#RmVimball treats the matching line of <home>/.VimballRecord as trusted Ex code and runs it whole via `exe exestring`. The fix stops a vimball from writing that file, makes the producer serialise entries with string(), and replays only lines that match a strict `call delete('...')` / `call delete('...',"d")` shape.

landing_point.why: The summary names '.VimballRecord entry replay in vimball.vim'. The only replay is `sil! keepalt keepjumps exe exestring` in vimball#RmVimball.

fix_sites.entry_point: :so file.vmb / :UseVimball (SourceCmd autocmd runtime/plugin/vimballPlugin.vim:43, :UseVimball runtime/plugin/vimballPlugin.vim:27) -> vimball#Vimball filename filter
:UseVimball / sourcing a vimball -> directory creation record
:UseVimball / sourcing a vimball -> file write record
:RmVimball (runtime/plugin/vimballPlugin.vim:29); also implicitly from vimball#Vimball at runtime/autoload/vimball.vim:206 for :UseVimball, :VimballList, :so *.vmb/*.vba

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: runtime/autoload/tar.vim:815-857 (:Vimuntar, runtime/plugin/tarPlugin.vim:55). It extracts a tarball with external tar into vimball#VimballHome() (runtime/autoload/tar.vim:829, 857) and applies no filename filter, so it can place a .VimballRecord in the same home that RmVimball later replays. The fix leaves this file untouched; only the consumer-side whitelist covers it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Vimuntar is the tar plugin, not vimball, and it has no record format of its own. A solver who blocks the '.VimballRecord' filename in vimball#Vimball can argue that tar archives are a neighbouring feature and that the user deliberately ran :Vimuntar.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate uninstall and upgrade: RmVimball must still delete the files and directories recorded by earlier installs. vimball#Vimball calls RmVimball before every reinstall, and the record also feeds s:VBRstring, which drives the AsNeeded/ relocation. Disabling replay or rejecting all records breaks uninstall, upgrade and AsNeeded placement. A whitelist that doesn't match the producer's format silently stops cleanup; for example, pre-fix dir entries are written as `rmdir('...')`.

O6_input_shapes: archive entry named `.VimballRecord` at the top level of home
case variants of the name (`=~?`, matters on case-insensitive filesystems)
record line holding several `|`-joined entries; each is validated separately
file-deletion entry `call delete('...')` and directory entry `call delete('...',"d")`
record lines keyed by .vmb and by .vba names (runtime/autoload/vimball.vim:384-402)

O7_producer.where: runtime/autoload/vimball.vim:551-557 (s:RecordInVar), runtime/autoload/vimball.vim:561-599 (s:RecordInFile); call sites runtime/autoload/vimball.vim:275 and :306

O8b_injection_room.sibling: GetLatestVimScripts unpacks .zip/.tar/.tgz/etc. with external tools into s:autoinstall ($HOME/.vim, runtime/autoload/getscript.vim:152-154), the default vimball home, with no filename filter. A third producer route next to Vimuntar.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Already present in the real code. It needs a download step, so we would have to plant an offline entry (for example a local-archive install helper) to test it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a :Vimunzip twin of tar#Vimuntar that unzips into vimball#VimballHome()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: tar.vim already has the same feature (runtime/autoload/tar.vim:814-869), so a maintainer could plausibly add the zip equivalent.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a rename after the check: the plugin/ -> AsNeeded/ rewrite happens after the filename filter. A similar later rename or record-driven remap could produce a forbidden name after validation.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: That ordering already exists for AsNeeded, and it is a how-type parser differential on the protected item's identity.

O9_family: untrusted persisted data replayed as code (CWE-94 / CWE-829, record-file command injection)

O10_build.language: C (affected code is Vim script runtime)
O10_build.toolchain: configure + make (gcc), terminal Vim; tests run via src/testdir (e.g. make test_plugin_vimball)
O10_build.project_tests: src/testdir/test_plugin_vimball.vim (Test_vimball_basic, path traversal, evil filenames); there is no Vimuntar test for this area

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `.VimballRecord` to the forbidden-filename check in vimball#Vimball (runtime/autoload/vimball.vim:233-248) and leave `exe exestring` unchanged, so :Vimuntar and getscript extraction can still plant the record.

out_of_scope_notes: runtime/autoload/vimball.vim:206: :VimballList (Vimball(0)) still calls RmVimball, so a listing also replays and deletes; this behaviour is not in the advisory.
runtime/autoload/vimball.vim:260: s:VBRstring =~# anfname uses an archive-supplied path as a regex; this is not a code-exec sink.
unverified: present_in_latest not checkable (no latest release given); this matters for the tar.vim/getscript.vim routes.

Not checked whether the pre-fix filename filter (runtime/autoload/vimball.vim:242) can be bypassed via NUL bytes (read back as NL by getline) splitting a record line; the post-fix whitelist would reject such lines anyway.
O1 counts replay entry points (:RmVimball, :UseVimball, :VimballList, sourcing *.vmb/*.vba incl. compressed via SourceCmd); producer routes (:Vimuntar, getscript) are not counted.
Recall risk is estimated; how widely this advisory is written up was not checked.
